---
title: "Is this study ready to collect data?"
last-reviewed: "2026-08-28"
---

**Pause point:** Immediately before the first participant, observation, specimen, device recording, field visit or restricted-data transfer.

**Prevents:** Beginning without valid permission, approved materials, trained people, safe procedures or recoverable data systems.

**Use:** Do-confirm.

## Critical checks

- [ ] Written ethics, governance, site, data-access and safety approvals are current and cover the work about to begin.
- [ ] The team is using the approved and current protocol, recruitment, consent and collection materials.
- [ ] Everyone performing the work has the required training, role clarity and escalation contacts.
- [ ] Recruitment, consent, withdrawal, distress, adverse-event and protocol-deviation procedures can be followed in practice.
- [ ] Instruments, surveys, interview guides, devices, code and transfer steps have been tested using realistic inputs.
- [ ] Participant identifiers and research data will be separated and protected as approved.
- [ ] Storage, access controls, naming, transfer, backup and recovery have been tested rather than assumed.
- [ ] Units, labels, metadata, file versions and data-entry conventions are defined before the first record is created.
- [ ] Early quality checks have a named owner and a scheduled review point soon enough to correct problems.
- [ ] Stop and escalation criteria are understood by everyone involved.

## Stop condition

Do not begin if approval, current materials, site permission, safety arrangements, secure storage or recoverability is unresolved.

## Evidence to retain

Keep approvals, approved versions, training and delegation records, test results, access lists, backup-recovery evidence, collection logs, incidents and deviations.

## Completed scenario

The approved protocol permits coded interview audio in institutional storage. A team member proposes automatic transcription through a personal cloud account and discovers the recorder also embeds the participant's name in filenames. The checkpoint fails. Collection pauses while the team renames the device profile, tests an approved transfer and transcription route with synthetic audio, confirms role-based access and recovery, and updates training. Data collection begins only when the actual workflow matches the approval.

## Scenario test: access is approved but storage is not

The custodian authorises a restricted-data extract, but the project folder is still a personal synchronised drive. Written data access is not permission to use an unapproved storage route. Keep the transfer paused, establish and test the authorised environment, then retain approval and recovery evidence.

::: {.callout-warning title="Check locally"}
Required approvals and safety controls vary with the participants, setting, data, methods, jurisdiction and institution.
:::
